Critically, computeNet (index.html:1231-1250) computes net = gross - ded in full floating-point precision from the raw, unrounded gross and ded — it is not derived by subtracting two already-rounded whole-dollar numbers. What the finding calls a defect is that fmt() — used identically everywhere in this codebase (hero chips, Breakdown rows, YearList, etc.) — rounds each of several related, independently-meaningful currency figures to the nearest whole dollar for *display* only. That a rounded subtotal minus a rounded deduction can differ by $1 from the rounded total is an unavoidable, universal property of showing whole-dollar rounded figures for numbers that don't happen to round the same way (the same artifact appears on bank statements, invoices, and virtually every budgeting app that shows subtotal/tax/total as separately rounded whole-currency amounts). Nothing in CLAUDE.md, the wage-core invariant, or the smoke-test suite promises penny-exact (or dollar-exact) reconciliation between independently displayed chips — that's a bar the finding invents and then holds the code to. The claimed severity ("the app's credibility rests on the numbers closing") is a rhetorical overstatement of a $1 cosmetic rounding artifact in a whole-dollar display, not a wage-math correctness bug, and doesn't rise to something the owner needs to act on.

The only place `auth.uid()` is compared against a leg is the cosmetic "proposer's own legs start accepted" branch, which simply does nothing when the proposer isn't a party. The UI-constraint angle does not save it. The client filter is real -- `computeSwapSuggestions` keys posts by `is_mine ? 'me' : poster_key` and `doPropose` only forwards `sugg.legPostIds` from those suggestions -- but the server is the stated security boundary for this feature (CLAUDE.md: "Anonymity is enforced in Postgres (column grants + security-definer RPCs)"; the migration revokes raw INSERT on matches/legs precisely so that propose_swap is the sole, validated entry point). security-01#2.why:
Mechanism confirmed and the outcome is not documented as intended anywhere; the project's own artefacts say the opposite.

What the code does (supabase/migrations/001_swap_board.sql:245-265): propose_swap checks is_swap_member(g), 2-3 legs, and that each post is in-group and 'open'; it resolves each post's author into leg_user but never compares auth.uid() to any of them. The only "proposer is a party" logic is `if a = auth.uid() then ... accepted = true`, which silently no-ops when the caller authored nothing. The victims cannot even see who did it: the table grant is `select (id, group_id, status, created_at)` -- proposed_by is deliberately ungranted -- and the proposer, being a non-party, gets no match card and is blocked from match_details/decline. So the abuse is attribution-free, which is exactly what makes it worse than ordinary in-group mischief (a member can already post nonsense, but cannot otherwise make everyone else's posts vanish from the board).

Why it is not intended behaviour:
- The migration's own comment at :227 says the RPC "validates authorship, open-status and group membership". It validates author *lookup*, not that the caller is an author -- the comment states an intent the body does not implement.
- docs/swap-board.md frames the whole model around parties: matching is client-side and computeSwapSuggestions (index.html:1763) is documented as "find every trade that involves ME"; every emitted suggestion has a 'me' leg; the audit log lists "non-parties blocked from match_details/reveal_match" as a verified property but has no probe for a non-party *proposing*, so the 29/29 + 5/5 figures never covered this path. The BACKLOG item touching propose_swap (a "propose against this post" affordance) still has the caller as a leg and says "never weaken RLS".
- Nothing in CLAUDE.md, the design doc, or the backlog describes a broker/charge-nurse role that pairs two other people's posts.
